subject: Q3 delivery snapshot & risk heatmap — prep for executive readout
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Product roadmap / OKR check-in for QBR prep

Team —

As we align for the upcoming executive readout (week of Aug 24), here’s a concise snapshot from Product to seed the QBR narrative and the risks we should surface. I attached the OKR check-in notes with a few example customer callouts. Please review and flag anything you disagree with by EOD Wed.

Key initiatives and status
- Streaming API GA (OKR: GA adopters + latency SLO): beta stable; performance regressions seen on long-context streaming in 2 customer threads. Scope: GA target 2026-08-31. Risk: MED (integration tests failing intermittently).
- Dedicated autoscaling policy v2 (OKR: cost/throughput): rollout on staging complete; canary in prod next week. Scope: incremental rollout to Dedicated customers Sept. Risk: LOW-MED (policy tuning).
- Private VPC/on-prem delivery automation (OKR: enterprise self-serve): delivery blockers on KMS rotation and install docs. Scope: pilot deliveries for 2 customers in Sept. Risk: MED-HIGH (docs and infra checklist gaps).

Top delivery risks to call out in QBR
1) Kernel/driver regressions delaying Streaming GA — probability: 40% — impact: high. Requires immediate engineering focus + vendor escalation.
2) Documentation/ops checklist gaps for Private pilots — probability: 60% — impact: medium. Needs dedicated tech-writer + solutions engineer time.
3) Capacity headroom for Dedicated canaries — probability: 25% — impact: medium-high. Ops to provision buffer.

Suggested exec-level asks
- Approve a short-term budget to reserve buffer capacity (one-week burn) for canary safety.
- Sign off on a cross-functional war room if Streaming GA slips past Aug 31.
- Approval to delay one Private pilot by 2 weeks if KMS work is not complete.

Attachment: okr-checkin-notes.pdf (summary + raw OKR scores)

Laura Bennett
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Product roadmap / OKR check-in for QBR prep

On Mon, Aug 16, 2026 at 09:12 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> As we align for the upcoming executive readout (week of Aug 24), here’s a concise snapshot from Product to seed the QBR narrative and the risks we should surface.

Thanks Laura — useful framing. I want to add technical color and a short mitigation plan for the kernel/driver risk (Streaming GA).

Status & root cause (short)
- The regression surfaced in internal perf tests and two customer betas when sequences exceed 8k tokens and streaming is enabled.
- Root cause: a combination of a kernel memory allocator edge case (introduced in driver 5.12.9) and a fallback path in our batching layer. Repro is flaky which makes automated gating noisy.

Mitigations we’re executing
- Immediate: pin driver to 5.12.7 on canary hosts and re-run canaries (ETA 48h).
- Short term: backport allocator fix and add targeted fuzz tests for long-context streaming (ETA 7 days).
- Medium: extend canary window + realtime tracing to capture rare repros (ETA 2–3 weeks).

Impact to dates
- Streaming API GA: current GA target 2026-08-31 — realistic contingency: slip to 2026-09-10 if backport uncovers further issues. We’ll push hard to keep the original date but recommend surfacing the contingency in the QBR.

I attached a heatmap I produced with Hannah showing probability vs impact per initiative. See "20260820_delivery-risk-heatmap.xlsx".

Markus Klein
SVP Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Product roadmap / OKR check-in for QBR prep

Thanks Markus — adding ops view.

We can provision a 10% headroom pool in Dedicated for the canary window (two weeks) with minimal impact to customers, but I need an explicit budget sign-off for that buffer. If Streaming GA slips into early Sept and we need to extend the canary, we should keep the pool for an additional week.

Action: Jonas, can you confirm in the QBR asks whether we escalate to Finance for the buffer (approx $12k/week)?

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Infra Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Product roadmap / OKR check-in for QBR prep — consolidated action items

Thanks everyone — good thread. I’ll surface the highlighted contingency and budget ask to the exec team at the QBR. Quick consolidation so the readout is crisp: 

1) Streaming API GA (owner: Markus) — immediate actions: pin driver on canary hosts (48h), backport allocator fix (7d). QBR ask: approve contingency date (sep10).
2) Dedicated canary headroom (owner: Hannah) — action: provision 10% buffer for 2 weeks. QBR ask: approve $24k one-time buffer for canary (covers 2 weeks).
3) Private pilot docs & KMS (owner: Laura) — action: assign tech-writer and solutions engineer to close checklist items; recommended contingency: delay pilot by 2 weeks if KMS rotation not complete.
4) Customer comms (owner: Laura + Jonas) — action: share SLA/latency SLO summary with Acme by Tue, Aug 25.

Deliverables before QBR (Aug 24 readout)
- Risk heatmap & one-slide owner callouts (Markus) — due Aug 21 (attached).
- Exec-ready ask summary w/ budget numbers (Jonas) — due Aug 22 (I’ll circulate tonight).
- Customer readiness note + SLA summary (Laura) — due Aug 25 (for post-QBR follow-up).

Please update the QBR folder (link below) with your final slide + the attachment referenced. I’ll include these items in the executive packet. If anything changes materially, flag me immediately.
